title: Tree Diameter
summary: The diameter of a tree is the count of edges in the longest path within the tree.
statement: The diameter of a tree is the count of edges in the longest path within the tree. Given an undirected tree with n nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, and a 2D array of edges where each edge connects two nodes, determine the number of edges in the longest path.
constraints: edges form an undirected tree labeled zero through n-1.
The diameter is the greatest number of edges on a simple path.
Return zero for the one-vertex tree represented by no edges.
hints: A farthest vertex from any start is an endpoint of some diameter.
Traverse once to find that endpoint, then again to find its farthest distance.
In a tree, unique paths ensure the two-sweep endpoint property and exact edge distances.
editorial: In a tree, unique paths ensure the two-sweep endpoint property and exact edge distances.

tests.explanation: The path one-zero-two has two edges.
A longest path from three through one and four to five has four edges.
